summary.text: Ancient Greece was a civilization of culturally and linguistically related city-states, centered on the northeastern Mediterranean, lasting from the Greek Dark Ages to the end of classical antiquity.
Its city-states, called poleis, began to form in the 8th century BC, and the absence of powerful states plus mountains between settlements encouraged small independent cities.
Classical Greek culture, especially philosophy, strongly influenced Rome, which is why Classical Greece is generally considered the cradle of Western civilization.

facts.label: Unified once
facts.value: Only from 338 to 323 BC, under Macedon

facts.label: City-states form
facts.value: In the 8th century BC, opening the Archaic period

facts.label: Classical period
facts.value: From the Persian invasion in 480 BC to Alexander's death in 323 BC

facts.label: Hellenistic period
facts.value: From 323 to 146 BC, until the Roman conquest

facts.label: Father of history
facts.value: Herodotus, whose Histories named the whole field

items.prompt: Greek settlements sat in valleys cut off from each other by mountains, and no strong state remained after Mycenaean power collapsed. What political pattern would you expect?

options.label: One large kingdom ruling from a single capital
Many small self-governing city-states
A set of cities all ruled by one distant emperor
Scattered villages with no shared political life

items.explain: The lack of powerful states and the mountainous terrain that separated settlements encouraged small independent city-states.

items.prompt: Historians know far more about Athens than about most other Greek cities. What is the main reason?

options.label: Most surviving historians were Athenian or pro-Athenian
Athens was the only Greek city with a written language
Other cities' records were destroyed on purpose by Athens
Athens was the largest Greek city in every period

items.explain: The writers who followed Herodotus were mostly Athenian or pro-Athenian, so far more is known about Athens.

items.prompt: A student treats Herodotus as perfectly reliable because he is called the father of history. What is the fair response?

options.label: His title proves each of his claims was checked and confirmed
He wrote the oldest record of any kind in the ancient world
His work named the field, yet its accuracy is still debated
He wrote only about events of his own lifetime, so no doubt remains

items.explain: Herodotus' Histories gave the field its name, but the accuracy of his work is debated, and he reached about a century into the past.

items.prompt: A museum label dates a temple to the years from the Persian invasion of 480 BC to the death of Alexander the Great in 323 BC. Which era of Greek history is that?

options.label: The Archaic period
The Hellenistic period
The Greek Dark Ages
The Classical period

items.explain: The Classical period runs from the Persian invasion of Greece in 480 BC until Alexander's death in 323 BC.

items.prompt: Greece lost its power, yet its ideas reached much of Europe. What carried them there?

options.label: Greek city-states kept ruling those lands for centuries
Rome adopted Greek culture, especially philosophy, and spread variants of it
Macedon forced one Greek school system on every region
Greek traders alone brought them in, with no state involved

items.explain: Classical Greek culture, especially philosophy, influenced Rome, which propagated variants of it through the Mediterranean and much of Europe.

items.prompt: A Macedonian king marches east, and later Greek-style culture appears in Western Asia and Northern Africa. What explains this?

options.label: His conquests spread Greek culture, starting the Hellenistic period
Persian traders brought Greek customs home with them
Greek colonies settled there before the Archaic period
Rome moved Greek culture there before it had any influence

items.explain: Alexander's conquests spread Greek culture into Northern Africa and Western Asia, which is the Hellenistic period.
